gbm_population_evidence.quote: High-grade Glioma; Medulloblastoma; Diffuse Intrinsic Pontine Glioma; Diffuse Midline Glioma, H3 K27M-Mutant
Newly diagnosed pHGG/DMG/DIPG Patients must have histologically confirmed pediatric high-grade glioma (pHGG, WHO Grade 3 or 4) or diffuse midline glioma with altered H3K27 (DMG, WHO Grade 4).

gbm_population_flag.reason: Glioblastoma not named; pediatric high-grade glioma 'WHO Grade 3 or 4' could be read as including historical grade 4 glioma (D27C), which would make it mixed_glioma_gbm_named.

candidate_evidence.quote: The goal of this interventional study is to Assess the safety and tolerability of atovaquone in combination with standard radiation therapy (RT)
Research shows that Atovaquone can inhibit a protein called STAT3, which is involved in cancer cell survival and immune response suppression.

role_evidence.quote: New Diagnosis followed by 2 weeks (+/- 7 days) atovaquone followed by approx. 6 weeks Atovaquone + Radiotherapy

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: STAT3 inhibition; radiosensitisation in hypoxic tumours

source_quote.quote: diffuse midline glioma with altered H3K27 (DMG, WHO Grade 4)

coder_notes: Pediatric-focused trial (ages >2 to 25 in Stratum 2; stdAges CHILD, ADULT). Population pHGG/DMG/DIPG/medulloblastoma; glioblastoma never named. Stratum 1 label registered as 'Stratum 1:' (trailing colon as in record). H3K27 alteration defines the DMG entity (one of alternative entry diagnoses), not a requirement for all; coded eligibility, not candidate-matched. Stratum 2 includes relapsed and post-RT non-progressed patients; Stratum 2 arm lists radiation as intervention though description is atovaquone alone. Atovaquone is the only drug in both experimental strata; no control arm.
